title: The Group Chat of the quarry
premise: Petra Dravenmoor has spent twelve years holding her fractured family together from the shadows of Quarry Hollow, a rust-belt town where everyone's business travels through one group chat. When her best friend Marisol vanishes, leaving only a ring of keys and a trail of encrypted messages, Petra discovers Marisol was racing to expose the quarry company poisoning their water — and that winning the regional swim championship is the only way to earn the scholarship money and platform to finish what Marisol started. As Petra trains, investigates, and finally lets her siblings and neighbors become a true found family instead of burdens, she learns love against duty means refusing to choose between them. The story ends with Petra winning the championship not for escape but for leverage, forcing the quarry's closure, and finding Marisol alive in the flooded lower tunnels she'd been hiding in all along.
about_author: Y. M. Dunmore grew up in a fading mill town where the neighborhood kids communicated almost entirely through one chaotic group chat, an experience that shapes every story they tell. They write young adult fiction about fierce, overlooked kids who discover that belonging is something you build, not something you're granted.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Opening on a 4 a.m. routine — packing lunches, checking locks, managing three younger siblings while Mom works nights — Petra finds Marisol's house keys left deliberately on her windowsill with no note. The emotional beat is dread disguised as calm: Petra knows Marisol would never leave without telling her.

chapters.title: Read Receipts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Quarry Hollow group chat erupts with rumors about Marisol's disappearance; police call it a runaway. Petra scrolls their years of messages and notices Marisol had gone quiet about 'the project' weeks ago. Beat: guilt, as Petra realizes she'd stopped asking questions to keep her own life manageable.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Petra's POV with flashbacks. After Dad's death, twelve-year-old Petra made herself invisible so the family could survive — quitting swim team, declining friendships, becoming 'the responsible one.' Now Coach Okafor begs her to return for her final championship season. Beat: longing versus duty, the novel's central tension named aloud.

chapters.title: What the Little Ones Know
chapters.summary: Alternating POV among siblings Theo (14), June (11), and Sam (8). Each has noticed Petra cracking — skipped meals, red eyes, the missing best friend they adored. Beat: tenderness and friction as they argue about how to help her without making things worse.

chapters.title: The Locker She Never Opened
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Using Marisol's keys, Petra opens locker 117 at the community pool: inside are water samples, a burner phone, and a map of the quarry's lower tunnels marked in red. Beat: revelation — Marisol wasn't running away; she was investigating the quarry company's chemical dumping.

chapters.title: Coach Okafor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Petra and Coach. Coach offers to reinstate Petra on the team if she commits fully — morning practices, no exceptions. Petra calculates the impossible math of training, sibling care, and investigation. Beat: she says yes anyway, choosing to fight on two fronts rather than abandon either.

chapters.title: Group Chat, Off the Record
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV via chat logs and texts. Petra quietly recruits trusted chat members — Dev the mechanic's son, Priya the nurse's aide, old Mr. Calloway — forming a secret channel called 'the Deep End.' Beat: the first spark of found family, chosen and deliberate rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Water That Tastes Like Pennies
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confirms a cluster of illnesses near the quarry and helps Petra get samples tested off-book. Meanwhile Mom, exhausted, nearly catches Petra sneaking out. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Petra realizes silence is what the quarry counts on.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. First meet back after six years: Petra finishes last in her heat but feels more alive than she has in a decade. Rival swimmer Cass Whitlock taunts her, then oddly offers help. Beat: humiliation transmuted into hunger; Petra discovers she wants to win for herself, not just the plan.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Alternating Petra and Mom (Renata) POV. Renata reveals she's known about the dumping for years — it's why she took the night shift at the quarry's clinic, collecting quiet evidence. Beat: devastating relief; Petra learns her mother wasn't absent, she was fighting too, alone.

chapters.title: The Message in the Burner
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The burner phone buzzes: a partial message from Marisol's number — coordinates and the word 'TUNNELS' before it cuts off. Petra realizes Marisol may be alive, hiding where the company can't reach her. Beat: hope arriving like a panic attack; stakes transform from justice to rescue.

chapters.title: Cass Whitlock's Secret
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass's father is the quarry's operations manager; she's watched him lie for years. She offers Petra access to company files in exchange for being let into the truth. Beat: enemy-to-ally turn, showing belonging can be built even across battle lines.

chapters.title: Practice at Midnight
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Training montage chapter: midnight laps, siblings timing her splits from the bleachers, Dev fixing her shoulder with borrowed PT knowledge. Beat: joy — the rare chapter where duty and love stop competing and start compounding.

chapters.title: The Company Notices
chapters.summary: Mr. Calloway's POV. A quarry lawyer visits Calloway's shop with veiled threats; someone photographed Petra at the tunnels' entrance. The group debates going public early. Beat: paranoia and fracture — trust within the found family gets its first real test.

chapters.title: June Runs Away
chapters.summary: June's POV. Terrified by the threats, eleven-year-old June runs toward the tunnels to find Marisol herself. Petra tracks her using everything Marisol taught them. Beat: terror and fury collapsing into fierce love; Petra understands she can't protect anyone by keeping them small.

chapters.title: What Marisol Left Behind
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (interlude). Flashback chapters reveal Marisol's investigation, her discovery of the flooded lower gallery, and why she went dark: the company threatened her undocumented family. Beat: reframing — Marisol's disappearance was protection, not abandonment, mirroring Petra's own invisibility.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Regionals day: Petra swims the race of her life with her whole ragtag family in the stands and qualifies for the state championship — the platform she needs. But the company announces the quarry's 'expansion,' which will seal the tunnels permanently. Beat: triumph undercut by a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Into the Lower Gallery
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Petra, Cass, Dev, and Theo enter the tunnels during the expansion's chaos to find Marisol before the flooding seals her in. Beat: claustrophobic rising action; every skill each character built across the book becomes load-bearing.

chapters.title: The Flooded Room
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They reach Marisol, injured but alive, guarding her evidence drive as water rises. Petra must choose between carrying the drive or moving faster. Beat: climax of values — she refuses the choice, and her family arrives to carry both, together.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Two days later, hollow-eyed and grieving time, Petra swims states. She doesn't swim for escape anymore; she swims as the visible face of Quarry Hollow, scholarship and leverage in one. Beat: catharsis — winning the race that matters by no longer needing it to save her.

chapters.title: The Quarry Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The evidence goes public: Renata's clinic records, Cass's testimony, Marisol's drive. The expansion halts, the quarry faces closure, and Marisol's family is shielded by the town that finally shows up. Beat: justice earned collectively, never by one careful girl alone.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Renamed
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing. Summer: the chat is renamed 'the Shallows,' open now instead of hidden. Marisol is home, Mom sleeps nights, and Petra — still careful, but no longer invisible — teaches the little ones to swim in the clean river. Beat: belonging as a practice, not a prize.
